keyFindings.description: compactionPoolSize is not in ConnectionsPerProcess (still 86), and infra/gcp/dispatch.go dispatchConnectionsPerPod stays 86, so TestDispatchConnectionsPerPodIsTheServers cannot catch the new pool; the docs and CHANGELOG say 88.

foldRead commits and then folds up to 32 MiB per load with no connection held; at base the rooms pool (4) bounded concurrent load folds, now nothing does (cold reads of distinct documents, room loads).

A retry step that finds no aged row returns compactionDone even when young rows remain (later > 0), and note() drops a note while its room is in flight; both drop a room whose rows will come due, so the 15-minute / 16-row bound the PR body states becomes the hourly sweep's.

No Contract change census: docs.API loses CompactAll, outbox.Deps loses Docs and Leases, VersionedStore gains pgVersioned(), and doc_compaction_owed is a schema the previous release does not write during a roll.
memoryUpdates never checks ctx, so coldReadTimeout and Shutdown's deadline no longer interrupt a buffered fold.
noteStoredUpdates' oldest argument is unused, yet readStoredLog runs an extra min(version) subquery on every load to fill it.
Load and LoadDocument duplicate the read-then-foldRead-then-note sequence and already differ in how they wrap the empty-history commit error.
The queue and the sweep each map compactOutcome to retry/leave; and a failed forgetCompactionCandidate logs as a failed check.
Comment says every committed append notes its room; settlement-repair and block-id backfill appends through AppendUpdateTx do not.
Comment says 0136 creates doc_compaction_owed; it is 0137.
PgVersioned.Compact's comment says an older build sharing the database runs it; an older build runs its own binary's Compact.

notDefects: pending_authors.go passing 1000 lines: moving its room-load code now would conflict with the trees editing the same file (INFRA-556, INFRA-605); not a defect of this change.
A failed room's eviction waits for the lock while holding a compaction-pool connection: latency only, no deadlock (transactions never wait on recovery).
A compaction that fails the same way is retried at most once a minute, logged each time: no error is hidden.
